source.title: The Dynamics of Gradient Descent for Overparametrized Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes gradient-descent convergence and zero squared training loss for an overparameterized shallow ReLU network, a related test of training convergence, but it does not use classification error or the benchmark settings in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theorem-level convergence results for zero squared training loss and one synthetic experiment on distance to a linearized minimum-norm solution. The cited Du et al. zero-loss result is prior work, not an experimental result of this paper; its own zero-loss theorem statement is recorded below. Figure-only distance plots are not extracted as numeric outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses previously established zero squared-loss convergence to prove proximity to a linearized minimum-norm solution and derive generalization bounds. Its own theory and synthetic regression experiment do not test any stated version: V1 concerns convolutional-network classification, V2 concerns spurious minima in teacher-student problems, and V4 concerns initialization comparisons affecting speed or trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. More precisely, the authors show convergence close to the linearized interpolator minimizing displacement from initialization, and use this characterization to derive noiseless generalization guarantees through an alternative proof of earlier results.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with fixed random-sign output weights, Gaussian input-weight initialization, and squared loss, deriving convergence bounds and testing a synthetic regression example. It does not run the CIFAR classification recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical guarantees depend on width, initialization, learning rate for discrete time, and the stated bounded-data and nonparallel-input assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 3 and 4 bound the distance between gradient-descent weights and the nearest zero-loss solution of the linearized network, with residual bounds decreasing as width increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In sufficiently wide shallow ReLU regression networks under the stated assumptions, gradient descent converges close to the minimum-displacement interpolator of the network linearized at initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 reports that distance to the linearized solution decreases with width across m = 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000; distance from initialization shows no clear width trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing width improves agreement with the linearized minimum-displacement solution in the tested synthetic regression setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Learning for Dynamics & Control; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, volume 144
record.problems: The empirical experiment uses a synthetic regression dataset and reports distances to a linearized solution, not classification error. The zero-loss statements in Lemma 2 and Lemma 10 are attributed to prior work rather than newly measured results. The paper does not report a benchmark classification experiment.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 plots distance measures for widths m = 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000 on the synthetic dataset, but exact values are figure-only and the paper describes the plotted behavior in text without numerical values. No numeric figure-only rows were added.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam, CIFAR classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated smaller-model and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student spurious-local-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh initialization, and Fixup.
Comparative initialization effects on learning speed, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, divergence, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The cited zero-loss lemmas are premises, not new findings of this study. The synthetic distance plots are already declared in rows_left_out and do not measure any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Tests zero squared training loss for overparameterized single-hidden-layer ReLU networks under stated assumptions. Does not test classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.

rows.subject: continuous-time gradient descent algorithm
rows.operation_detail: Continuous-time gradient descent on summed squared loss; output weights a_k are fixed random signs and input weights initialize as stated.

conditions.value: w_k(0) ∼ N(0, κ²I_d), κ = 1; a_k independently ±1 with probability 1/2
n bounded data points; no two x_i are parallel

rows.value: The algorithm achieves zero loss with probability greater than 1 − δ; loss converges exponentially, ‖f(t) − Y‖ ≤ exp(−ct/4)‖f₀ − Y‖.
rows.uncertainty: Probability greater than 1 − δ over initialization
rows.locator: Section 3.1, Lemma 2; cited as Du et al. (2019b)
rows.note: Although Lemma 2 is explicitly attributed to Du et al. (2019b), it is stated as a theorem premise in this paper. It is zero squared loss, not classification error.
rows.check: Lemma 2 is explicitly attributed to Du et al. (2019b), so it should not be a result row for this study. Its zero squared-loss guarantee concerns a shallow fully connected ReLU network, not V1's convolutional-network classification error. Zero loss is an asymptotic convergence statement.

rows.subject: discrete-time gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on summed squared loss with fixed random-sign output weights and Gaussian initialization of input weights.

conditions.value: w_k(0) ∼ N(0, κ²I_d), κ = 1; a_k independently ±1 with probability 1/2
bounded data; no two data points are parallel

rows.value: The discrete-time algorithm achieves zero loss.
rows.uncertainty: With probability more than 1 − δ over initialization
rows.note: This is an explicitly cited prior result included in the proof section, rather than a new experiment by this paper.
rows.check: Lemma 10 is explicitly attributed to Du et al. (2019b), so it should not be a result row for this study. The extracted width confuses Theorem 4 with Lemma 10: Lemma 10 requires m = Ω(d⁴Cᵧ²n⁶/(c⁴δ³)); the stronger extracted width belongs to the paper's bound on distance to the linearized solution. The locator should be Section 10, Lemma 10, before Section 10.0.1. Squared-loss convergence does not measure V1's classification effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
